title: resilient-egress-throttle-and-graceful-fallback-fix
author: Elena Brooks
release_notes: Fix: Smooth egress throttle to prevent circuit flip loops; add slow-rejoin backoff and new telemetry for SLO breach investigation.
body:
Context: During a regional egress saturation incident (SUP-8042) we observed repeatable circuit flips and tenant failovers when backend egress caps were hit. The symptom was a short storm of traffic (spike + uneven egress shaping) that caused rapid circuit open/close cycles and then a cascade of regional failovers. This PR implements a short, targeted hotfix: an egress throttle smoothing layer and a slow-rejoin backoff for circuits to avoid oscillation. Motivation: improve reliability under bursty egress constraints, reduce churn on the SLO enforcement path, and make regional failover events less noisy.

What I changed (high level):
- Introduced an egress_throttle_coordinator that performs exponential smoothing on instantaneous egress usage and emits an adjusted throttle target (new module: pkg/runtime/egress/throttle_coordinator.go).
- Added a slow_rejoin_backoff to the circuit manager so once a circuit transitions to OPEN it waits with an exponentially increasing probe interval before attempting to rejoin (pkg/runtime/circuit/manager.go).
- Hooked the smoothing signals into routing policy so the smart router can prefer spare capacity routes instead of immediately failing over (pkg/router/policy.go).
- Improved telemetry: new metrics and tags (slo.egress.smoothed_target, circuit.rejoin_delay_ms, circuit.rejoin_attempts) and a validation probe that stamps tenant id and region for postmortem (internal/telemetry/metrics.yaml + runtime/telemetry/instrumentation.py).
- Small docs and runbook update for incident responders (docs/runbooks/egress-throttle-surge.md).

Detailed commit summary:
- Commit 1: add throttle_coordinator with smoothing algorithm + unit tests (smoothing parameters configurable via env/runtime flags).
- Commit 2: integrate smoothing into router policy and add an adaptive margin to reduce unnecessary cross-region egress.
- Commit 3: add slow_rejoin_backoff to circuit manager with deterministic unit tests and simulation harness scenarios.
- Commit 4: add telemetry counters, tag propagation, and update Grafana dashboard JSON (telemetry changes are additive only).
- Commit 5: runbook and docs + minor lint fixes.

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/runtime/egress/throttle_coordinator.go (new)
- pkg/runtime/circuit/manager.go (modified)
- pkg/router/policy.go (modified)
- runtime/telemetry/instrumentation.py (modified)
- docs/runbooks/egress-throttle-surge.md (new)
- observability/dashboards/egress-throttle-dashboard.json (modified)

Testing and CI: All unit tests and integration smoke tests passed in CI (linux/amd64, linux/arm64). Added a small simulation test in the existing harness to replay the incident pattern; simulation verifies no repeated immediate rejoin attempts and that smoothed target avoids cross-region panic. CI summary: build ✓, unit-tests ✓, integration-smoke ✓, lint ✓, e2e-sim (new) ✓. Post-merge we ran a staged canary in a low-traffic region for 2 hours before full rollout.

Backward compatibility and safety: The smoothing parameters are behind a runtime flag and default to conservative values (alpha=0.25, min_rejoin_ms=500, max_backoff_ms=60000). The telemetry additions are additive and do not change any existing metric names. No breaking changes.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Aisha Patel (reviewer): "This looks good overall; two requests: (1) add a small doc blurb explaining the tuning knobs and safe defaults; (2) ensure the backoff uses jitter to avoid thundering herd." 
- Author (Elena): "Added docs + jitter in commit 3. Jitter is triangular with a ±15% window; added unit test to assert jitter bounds in simulation harness." 
- Marco Li (reviewer): "Can we add an emergency override so ops can set throttle target to manual during maintenance?" 
- Author: "Added env var REDWOOD_EGRESS_THROTTLE_OVERRIDE in commit 5. It's gated by the ops role and logged as an audit event." 
- Claire Nguyen (approver): "Verified metrics in the staging run; behavior looks stable. Approving pending CI." 

CI reruns: one flaky test (router/policy_test) failed on first run due to a timing assertion; fixed by switching to condition-wait and re-run. All green after fix.

Risk and mitigation: The change touches routing and circuit manager paths which are sensitive. To mitigate: feature gated, rolled out to 10% of regions first, health check monitor (SLO delta > 0.5% triggers automatic rollback), and added an alert threshold on circuit.rejoin_attempts that will page SRE if spikes occur.

Merge & rollout: Merged via squash-merge after approvals. Rollout plan: 10% regions -> 50% -> global over 6 hours if no regressions. During canary we observed 27% reduction in immediate rejoin attempts and 12% reduction in cross-region failover events for the test tenant cohort.

Follow-ups: 
- ENG-1830: Tune smoothing alpha per-tenant workload profiles (tracking ticket created).
- Telemetry follow-up to add a correlation view on egress throttle vs token cost per request (low-priority).

Related tickets and references: SUP-8042 (support ticket), internal incident writeup: https://linear.app/redwood/incident/INC-2025-012-1, and the proposed SLO runbook change PR # (linked in runbook). 

If anything goes sideways during rollout, ops can flip REDWOOD_EGRESS_THROTTLE_OVERRIDE to set a static throttle target, or roll back the release using the rollback pipeline documented in docs/runbooks/rollback.md.
merge: merged by Claire Nguyen after approvals. Canary rollout observed expected stabilization; full rollout completed per plan.
